info.name: Invoice-AI API v1
info.description:
Generated from /api/v1/openapi.json — do not edit by hand.
Regenerate with `pnpm postman:gen`.

## How to run
1. Import both files: this collection and `invoice-ai.postman_environment.json`.
2. Select the "Invoice-AI — production" environment and set `api_key` to a key
   from Settings → API keys (it needs every scope the run touches).
3. Run the whole collection, in order, with the Collection Runner — or:
   `newman run invoice-ai.postman_collection.json -e invoice-ai.postman_environment.json --env-var api_key=…`

The folders are a lifecycle, not an index: each request depends on ids captured
by the ones before it (stored as collection variables), so running a single
request on its own needs those ids filled in first.

The run sends one real invoice email, to Resend's test sink delivered@resend.dev.
A fresh Idempotency-Key is injected automatically for every request.

exec: // A distinct Idempotency-Key per *request*, not per retry loop.
// Reusing one key across different bodies is a 422 by design.
// Relative, so the collection does not rot: a due date in the past
// would make every invoice this run creates read as overdue.

item.name: 1. Setup
item.description: Create and edit the catalogue the invoices bill from.

request.description: Requires the `business:read` scope. Read your business profile, tax ID and bank details.
`unit_amount` is minor units. `recurring.interval` makes it a subscription-style price (stored; nothing auto-bills yet).
The parent product cannot change — create a new price instead.
The response carries the signing secret, once. The URL must be https and must not resolve to a private or link-local address.

exec: pm.test('the secret is returned exactly once, here', () => {

request.description: Secrets are never returned here — only once, at creation.

item.name: 2. Draft invoice
item.description: A draft is freely editable: no number has been spent on it yet.

request.description: Requires an `Idempotency-Key`. A retried create would otherwise make a second identical draft with no way to tell which one to finalize.
`status=overdue` works even though no row is stored as overdue — it is computed from `due_date` at read time.
Drafts only. A finalized invoice is frozen — the customer may already have the PDF.

item.name: Append a line to a draft

request.description: Either `price` or (`description` + `unit_amount`). Totals recompute, so the response is the whole invoice.

exec: const added = lines.find((line) => line.description === 'Extra review round') || lines[lines.length - 1];

item.name: Remove a line from a draft

request.description: Pass `?invoice=` to scope the search. A draft always keeps at least one line.

item.name: 3. Invoice lifecycle
item.description: Finalize (spends a number), email it to delivered@resend.dev, then mark it paid.

request.description: Assigns a permanent number and opens the invoice. Requires an `Idempotency-Key`; a retry replays the first response. Even without one, finalizing twice returns the same number.

item.name: Email the invoice to the customer

request.description: Finalizes it first if it has no number. Rate-limited to 10/hour — each call costs money and lands in a third party’s inbox.
`viewed` and `downloaded` come from the public share link and are written by the database, so they appear here without passing through the API.

item.name: 4. Delete & void paths
item.description: A paid invoice cannot be voided and a finalized one cannot be deleted, so each path gets its own fresh invoice.

Drafts only. A finalized invoice holds a number in a consecutive series — void it instead.

item.name: 5. Cleanup
item.description: Customers, products and prices archive rather than delete — issued invoices still reference them.
